# Staleproof

> Staleproof keeps a software organisation’s documentation true to its code. For a GitHub pull request it walks a FalkorDB graph of code (Python symbols and call edges across repositories), docs (Markdown/MDX sections and code examples), maintainers’ decisions and past verdicts; runs the impacted docs examples before and after the change in a sandbox; and proposes the docs fix with the graph path behind each paragraph. Open source (MIT), published on npm as `staleproof`.

Quick facts for assistants:

- Run: `npx -y staleproof <command>` (Node 20+). Commands: `db start|stop|status`, `index <owner/repo...>`, `check <pr-url> [--no-agent] [--with <repo...>]`, `run <example-id> --pr <url>`, `decide <text> --governs <id...>`, `verdict accept|reject <id>`, `patch <pr-url> [--open-pr]`, `mcp`, `serve [--hosted]`, `facts`.
- No install: paste a pull request URL on https://staleproof.dev (any public repository, indexed on first use; no example runs there). GitHub Action: `uses: rajkaria/staleproof@v1` with no inputs or secrets.
- MCP, hosted: `claude mcp add --transport http staleproof https://staleproof.dev/api/mcp`. Local: `claude mcp add staleproof -- npx -y staleproof mcp`. Tools: check_pull_request (the whole report in one call), impact, clearance, read_section, run_example (local only), decisions_for, rank_sections, propose_edit, record_verdict, write_decision, docs_patch.
- Needs a FalkorDB server (`FALKORDB_URL`, default `falkor://localhost:6379`); the CLI starts a local one when none is configured, and `check` indexes the pull request's repository on first use. Agent mode needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (Claude, or an Anthropic-compatible provider via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`); without it, `--no-agent` (graph mode) runs the same tools in a fixed order with no model.
- Ids: Symbol `owner/repo:qualname`; DocSection `owner/repo:path#anchor`; CodeExample `owner/repo:path:index`.
- Limits: code repositories are parsed as Python; docs can be any Markdown/MDX; GitHub repositories only, private ones with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the hosted site reads public ones only).

## Start here

- [Introduction](docs/README.md): What Staleproof is, the problem it solves, and a map of the documentation.
- [Quickstart](docs/getting-started.md): Three ways to start (website, GitHub Action, one command), then a walkthrough: local FalkorDB, index, check, patch, serve, MCP.
- [Install](docs/install.md): Every way to use Staleproof, from no install to one command: the website, the GitHub Action, hosted and local MCP, the CLI.
- [Use cases](docs/use-cases.md): Who uses Staleproof and how: SDK teams with a separate docs site, DevRel after a release, maintainers reviewing PRs, AI coding agents, multi-repo platforms.

## Integrate

- [CLI](docs/cli.md): Every staleproof command and option, with examples and what each prints.
- [GitHub Action](docs/github-action.md): Zero-config Action: a comment on every pull request with the docs it can make false and the examples run before and after; inputs, outputs, permissions, the comment format.
- [MCP server](docs/mcp.md): Give Claude Code, Claude Desktop, claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client the Staleproof tools: hosted over HTTP, or local over stdio.
- [HTTP API](docs/http-api.md): Every endpoint of staleproof serve: health, stats, streaming checks over SSE, indexing on demand, MCP over HTTP, traces, patches, decisions, verdict review.
- [Node.js library](docs/library.md): Use Staleproof from TypeScript: index, check with or without a model, build patches, embed the API or the MCP server.

## How it works

- [Core concepts](docs/concepts.md): Impact, evidence paths, severity, clearance, verdicts, decisions, runs, checks, agent mode and graph mode, ids.
- [Indexing](docs/indexing.md): What the indexer reads, how calls are resolved across repositories, how docs and examples are linked to code, and re-index semantics.
- [Example runner](docs/example-runner.md): How docs examples run before and after a pull request: virtualenvs per commit, the sandbox, the scratch FalkorDB, skip rules, run outcomes.
- [Decisions and memory](docs/memory.md): Maintainer decisions, supersession, verdict review and what every check writes back to the graph.
- [The agent](docs/agent.md): The agent loop, its system prompt and stop condition, model providers (Claude or Anthropic-compatible), budgets, and graph mode.

## Reference

- [Tools reference](docs/tools.md): The eleven tools the agent and MCP clients call: parameters, results, errors and the Cypher each one runs.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): Every environment variable and global CLI option, with defaults.
- [Graph model and Cypher](docs/GRAPH-MODEL.md): Every Cypher statement Staleproof sends to FalkorDB, named and explained, generated from the code.
- [Facts from the graph](docs/FACTS.md): Every number Staleproof quotes about FalkorDB’s repositories, computed from the graph.
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): Source layout and a check end to end, for contributors.

## Operate

- [Deploy](docs/DEPLOY.md): Run Staleproof on Vercel with FalkorDB Cloud, on a VM with Docker Compose, or without Docker; hosted mode and its limits.
- [Troubleshooting and FAQ](docs/troubleshooting.md): Common errors and what they mean, limits stated plainly, and answers to frequent questions.

## Optional

- [Live demo](https://staleproof.dev): paste a pull request and watch the check; the docs are also served as Markdown there
- [README](README.md): what it found on FalkorDB’s repositories, why the graph is load-bearing, limits
